headline: Commercial property tax shift set at 1.03; $132,000 state grant to refresh HarborWalk accepted.
summary: Public Works gave an update on the wastewater treatment plant upgrade at 50 Essex Ave. No vote was taken on that item. Members also approved the fiscal 2027 tax shift, accepted a $132,000 state grant, and removed the newspaper publication requirement for fee changes.
decisions: Approved the appointment of Angela Sanfilippo to the Fisheries Commission, 9 to 0.
Approved the consent agenda, as amended, 9 to 0.
Referred to the Planning and Development Committee and the planning board, with abutter notice waived and a public hearing set for December 8th, 2026, 9 to 0.
Approved accepting a $132,000 Massachusetts Downtown Initiative capital grant to refresh the HarborWalk, 8 to 1.
Approved accepting a framed portrait of former city clerk Joanne Senos, valued at about $150, 8 to 0 with 1 recused.
Withdrew, without prejudice, a proposal to raise the minimum lot area per dwelling unit in the RC40 Coastal Residential district from 20,000 to 40,000 square feet, 9 to 0.
Denied a motion to set a tax factor of one, equal rates for all property classes; it failed, with 2 in favor and 7 opposed.
Approved a residential tax factor of 0.9973, a 1.03 shift to commercial and industrial property, for fiscal 2027, 8 to 0 with 1 opposed.
Approved removing the requirement to publish fee changes in a local newspaper, 8 to 0 with 1 absent.
discussion: Tax classification: Speakers from the business community urged keeping the 1.03 shift, and one resident urged 1.05. Members debated a factor of one for equal rates against the 1.03 shift.
HarborWalk grant: Members asked about the wayfinding signs, the thermoplastic markers, and effects on the working waterfront. Concerns were raised about public input before grants are applied for.
Wastewater plant upgrade: Members asked about cost, the construction schedule, piling, odor control, and cyber security at the plant. Staff answered each question.
